title: Prime-to-ell alteration coverings persist under sufficiently close approximation
statement: Let $(A,\mathfrak m)$ be an excellent henselian Noetherian local domain, put $S=\operatorname{Spec}A$ and $\widehat S=\operatorname{Spec}\widehat A$, and let $\ell$ be a prime invertible in $A$ [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Write $\widehat A=\varinjlim_\alpha A_\alpha$ as the directed union of finite type $A$-subalgebras, with inclusions $s_\alpha:A_\alpha\to\widehat A$. Let $(X_i\to\widehat S)_{i\in I}$ be a finite covering family in $\operatorname{alt}/\widehat S$ for the topology of $\ell'$-alterations [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. For any finite type model $(X_{i,\alpha_0}\to\operatorname{Spec}A_{\alpha_0})_i$ of this family [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], there exist $\alpha_1\geq\alpha_0$ and $N_0\geq1$ such that for all $\alpha\geq\alpha_1$, $N\geq N_0$, and $A$-algebra maps $u:A_\alpha\to A$ congruent to $s_\alpha$ modulo $\mathfrak m^N\widehat A$, the schemes $X_{i,u}$ pulled back along $\operatorname{Spec}u$ have finite generic fibres, and the family $(X_{i,u}^{\mathrm{dom}}\to S)_i$ is a covering family in $\operatorname{alt}/S$. Here $X_{i,u}^{\mathrm{dom}}$ is the reduced closed union of the irreducible components of $X_{i,u}$ dominating $S$ [def-weil-irreducible-components], [def-pc-reduced-scheme]; empty members may be omitted. No regularity or boundary hypothesis is imposed on the $X_i$.

source.place: Expose III Proposition 3.1(i),(iii), pp.37--38, applied to the finite disjoint union of the family. A fixed sufficiently high model suffices; auxiliary proper/Nisnevich covering certificates descend further as in Lemma 3.1.1.

proof.text: The completion $\widehat A$ is a domain by [lem-per-henselian-excellent-completion-domain]. It is Noetherian and complete for $\mathfrak m\widehat A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-completion-noetherian-quotient-noetherian] (the ideal $\mathfrak m$ is finitely generated and $A/\mathfrak m$ is a field), and is local with that maximal ideal by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring]. Thus it is excellent by [lem-per-complete-local-excellence]. Invertibility of $\ell$ persists under a ring map. Apply [lem-per-alteration-cover-proper-normal-form] over $\widehat S$: obtain a proper surjection $p:P\to\widehat S$ with $P$ integral, of function-field degree $\delta>0$ prime to $\ell$, a finite completely decomposed separated etale family $v_j:V_j\to P$, and maps $h_j:V_j\to X_{i(j)}$ over $\widehat S$. These schemes are finite type over $\widehat S$.

source.place: III 3.1, p.37 opening observation and p.38 standard refinement; I 6.3(ii); II 3.2.1

proof.text: All finite type schemes over the Noetherian bases in this argument are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Their structure maps are locally of finite presentation by [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth]; finite type also supplies quasi-compactness. Thus they are of finite presentation, even when the given $X_i$ are not separated. Apply the object part of [thm-pd-spreading-out] to $P$ and the finitely many $V_j$, keeping the prescribed models of the $X_i$. Increase the index to a common stage. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-diagram-lift-of-models] to descend all $v_j,h_j$ and their relations over the base, with these fixed object models. By [lem-weil-pbc-eventually-proper] increase the stage so $p_\alpha:P_\alpha\to S_\alpha$ is proper. By [lem-per-nisnevich-cover-limit-descent] increase it again so $(v_{j,\alpha})_j$ is completely decomposed etale. These properties hold at every later stage: properness is preserved by base change [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], and the Nisnevich node explicitly gives the later-stage assertion.

source.place: III section 2, p.36; III 3.1 and Lemma 3.1.1, p.38

proof.text: Write $\widehat K=\operatorname{Frac}\widehat A$. Each $X_i$ is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/\widehat S$, so condition (i) of [lem-per-generic-fibre-finiteness-criterion] holds and its generic fibre is finite over $\widehat K$. For $P$: its generic point maps to the generic point of $\widehat S$ because $p$ is surjective and that image generalizes every image point, and $\kappa(P)/\widehat K$ has degree $\delta$, so the same node makes $P_{\widehat\eta}$ finite. A point of $P_{\widehat\eta}$ has all its generizations in this finite discrete fibre, so it is the generic point of $P$; on an affine open its ring is a localization of a domain, hence $P_{\widehat\eta}=\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(P)$. Put $d_T$ the dimension of the finite algebra of $T_{\widehat\eta}$ for $T$ in the list $P,X_i$; thus $d_P=\delta$, and $d_{X_i}=0$ for empty members. View $\operatorname{Spec}\widehat K$ as the limit of the principal opens $D(b)$, $b\ne0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite-locally-free] to the finite-presentation $T\to\widehat S$: over some $D(a_T)$, $a_T\ne0$, it is finite locally free of degree $d_T$ (at the limit, a finite algebra over a field is free of its dimension). Enlarge the stage until every $a_T$ lies in $A_\alpha$; the rings $(A_\alpha)_{a_T}$ have direct limit $\widehat A_{a_T}$, and a second application of [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite-locally-free] to these localized models makes every $T_\alpha\vert_{D(a_T)}$ finite locally free of degree $d_T$ at one common stage.

source.place: III 3.1(i), pp.37--38: preserve finiteness and generic rank on principal opens; EGA permanence there, expressed by Stacks 06AC

proof.text: Fix such a common stage $\alpha_1\geq\alpha_0$. For each of the finitely many nonzero $a_T\in\widehat A$, choose $N_T\geq1$ for which its coordinate in $A/\mathfrak m^{N_T}$ is nonzero. Such a coordinate exists because the completion consists of compatible sequences [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Set $N_0=\max_TN_T$. If $\alpha\geq\alpha_1$, $N\geq N_0$, and $u$ is as in the statement, the two values of $a_T\in A_\alpha$ have the same image in $A/\mathfrak m^{N_T}$: their difference belongs to $\mathfrak m^N\widehat A$, which maps to zero in this quotient. Consequently $u(a_T)\ne0$ in $A$. The same witnesses and bound work for every later $\alpha$ by restricting $u$ to $A_{\alpha_1}$.

source.place: III 3.1(i), pp.37--38, choosing n so a is nonzero modulo the corresponding power

proof.text: Write $K=\operatorname{Frac}A$. The generic-point map $\operatorname{Spec}K\to S_\alpha$ induced by $u$ lies in every $D(a_T)$. Therefore the generic fibre of $T_u$ is finite and has coordinate-algebra dimension $d_T$: by [def-pc-finite-locally-free] its fibre at the image point has dimension $d_T$ over that point's residue field; extending this field to $K$ tensors a basis and keeps its dimension. Finiteness is equally explicit: that fibre is the spectrum of a finite-dimensional algebra, and after extension it is the spectrum of the tensor algebra. This proves finite generic fibres for all $X_{i,u}$ and for $P_u$, with $\dim_K\Gamma((P_u)_\eta,\mathcal O)=\delta$. Properness of $P_\alpha$ gives properness of $P_u$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence].

source.place: III 3.1(i),(iii), pp.37--38: generic fibre ranks after specialization

proof.text: Let $B=\Gamma((P_u)_\eta,\mathcal O)$; it is a finite-dimensional commutative $K$-algebra of dimension $\delta$. Choose a composition series as a $B$-module by repeatedly taking a proper submodule of maximal $K$-dimension; dimensions strictly decrease. Each simple quotient is $B/\mathfrak q$ for a maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$: a nonzero vector generates a simple module and its annihilator is maximal. Additivity of dimension gives $\delta=\sum_a[B/\mathfrak q_a:K]$, with repetitions permitted. Since $\ell\nmid\delta$, at least one summand has degree prime to $\ell$. The corresponding point of the finite generic fibre gives an irreducible component of $P_u$ dominating $S$; it is a component because all points of that generic fibre are minimal as well as maximal. In $(P_u)^{\mathrm{dom}}$ its residue field remains $B/\mathfrak q_a$. The dominant-parts node gives that $(P_u)^{\mathrm{dom}}$ is reduced, finite type, and has all generic residue extensions finite. It is a closed subscheme of $P_u$, hence proper over $S$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. Its proper image is closed [def-weil-proper-morphism] and contains the generic point of the integral $S$, so it is surjective. Thus it is a proper surjective maximally $\ell'$-finite object and a singleton covering by [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology].

source.place: III 3.1(iii), p.38, selecting a prime-to-ell component after approximation; generic Artinian algebra dimension argument written out

proof.text: The specialized family $V_{j,u}\to P_u$ is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change], applied to the completely decomposed family at stage $\alpha$. It is completely decomposed: for $p_u\mapsto p_\alpha$, a residue-preserving point above $p_\alpha$ pulls back to a $\kappa(p_u)$-rational point because $\kappa(p_\alpha)\otimes_{\kappa(p_\alpha)}\kappa(p_u)=\kappa(p_u)$. By [lem-per-finite-generic-dominant-parts], applied to $T=P_u$, every $V_{j,u}$ has finite generic fibre, so (same node) every $V_{j,u}^{\mathrm{dom}}$ is an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S$, and the base-changed family $(V_{j,u}\times_{P_u}P_u^{\mathrm{dom}}\to P_u^{\mathrm{dom}})_j$ is completely decomposed; it is etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change]. By the etale clause of [lem-per-dominant-part-coreflection] (for integral $S$ its $X_{\mathrm{md}}$ is $X^{\mathrm{dom}}$), this family is $(V_{j,u}^{\mathrm{dom}}\to P_u^{\mathrm{dom}})_j$ with the functorial restrictions of $v_{j,u}$. A completely decomposed etale family is $\ell'$-decomposed (degree one), so it covers by [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology]. Compose it with the proper singleton covering in Step 6, using [lem-per-alteration-cover-calculus], to obtain a covering family $(V_{j,u}^{\mathrm{dom}}\to S)_j$ of $S$.

source.place: III 3.1(iii) and Lemma 3.1.1, p.38: the Nisnevich leg after specialization and dominant reduction

proof.text: The specialized maps $h_{j,u}:V_{j,u}\to X_{i(j),u}$ are morphisms of finite type $S$-schemes, so the functoriality of $X\mapsto X_{\mathrm{md}}$ in [lem-per-dominant-part-coreflection] restricts them to $S$-maps $V_{j,u}^{\mathrm{dom}}\to X_{i(j),u}^{\mathrm{dom}}$. Every $X_{i,u}$ has finite generic fibre by Step 5, so [lem-per-finite-generic-dominant-parts] makes each target an object of $\operatorname{alt}/S$. The covering of Step 7 therefore refines the family of these targets; its generated covering sieve is contained in their generated sieve. Upward closure of covering sieves, part of [def-per-prime-to-ell-alteration-topology], proves that $(X_{i,u}^{\mathrm{dom}}\to S)_i$ covers. Empty members contribute no maps from nonempty schemes and may be omitted. The threshold and index were chosen before $\alpha,N,u$, so all required quantifiers hold.

source.place: III 3.1(iii), p.38, functorial diagram and covering refinement
